REAL ESTATE

30-Year Fixed: 7.29% -0.06  |  15-Year Fixed: 6.95% -0.05

Renting is the cheaper move, and here by a mile. Zillow's latest report puts the typical U.S. rent at $1,932 a month in September, while a new buyer's payment, with 10% down and taxes and insurance included, is $3,037. That is $1,105 more every month to own, and rental demand is up 19.2% from a year ago as would-be buyers rent instead.

Here at home. In Zillow's San Francisco metro, which includes Oakland, Fremont and Hayward, rent is $3,445 against an $8,931 buyer payment, $5,486 apart. In the San Jose metro, which includes Milpitas, it is $3,812 against $11,845, so the payment would cover the rent three times over. Our two metros lead the country in rental demand growth: San Jose is up 82.5% from a year ago and San Francisco 66.9%.

Rents are catching up. San Francisco metro rent is up 11.8% in a year while the buyer payment rose 7.1%; nationally it is the other way around. On our own MLS, Fremont's median asking price of $1,300,000 works out to about $8,000 a month in principal and interest alone at today's 7.29% with 10% down, before taxes and insurance.

What it means for you. Renting wins month one, so buying here is a bet on equity and on staying put. If you rent and are weighing a purchase, compare both paths over five to ten years, not one month, with metro rents climbing about 10% a year. If you are selling, your buyer is often a renter doing exactly that math, so a price that pencils against today's rent gets the call.

Rates and the Fed. Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average eased to 7.29% today from 7.35%, and the 15-year is 6.95%, after the Fed held its rate Wednesday (more in Economy).

Today's count. Board wide: 2,558 listings across the 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, up from 2,554, with 141 coming soon and 139 brand new. The five city ledger carries 670 live listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City, 601 on the market and 69 coming soon, down from 674.

Fremont holds 225 live listings: 179 active, 29 coming soon and 17 brand new, with a median on market list price of $1,300,000 at $808 a square foot and a typical listing out 35 days. Hayward carries 193 (from 196), Milpitas 103, Newark 89 and Union City 60 (all unchanged). Across all five cities the median is $1,079,000 at $668 a square foot, 282 homes are priced under a million, and 180 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

STOCKS

S&P 500: 7,743.98 +0.28%  |  Dow: 52,475.10 +0.19%  |  Nasdaq: 26,549.85 +0.27%

Alphabet stumbles. The numbers above are Wednesday's closes. As of 11:23 AM PT Alphabet is down 13.2% after its earnings and the Nasdaq is down 1.59%. Revenue rose 25% and Google Cloud grew 103%, but spending on AI data centers more than doubled to $51.4 billion in the quarter and free cash flow turned negative. Microsoft's Azure grew 48%, and its stock is down 0.35%. Over six months through Wednesday, Microsoft was up 25.1% and Alphabet down 7.3%.

ECONOMY

10-Year Treasury: 5.05% +0.06  |  Gold: $4,081.20 +0.20%  |  Silver: $54.04 -0.83%  |  Brent Crude: $115.32 +1.26%

The Fed holds. The Fed kept its target range at 3.75% to 4.00% Wednesday, after raising it in September. Two policymakers, Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack, voted against the decision because they wanted another hike, and the statement says inflation "remains elevated." The next meeting is in December.

Rates watch the 10-Year. Mortgage rates follow the 10-Year Treasury more closely than the Fed's own rate. It closed Wednesday at 5.05%, up from 4.99%, and is near 4.99% this morning. Brent's December contract settled up 1.26% at $115.32, gold rose 0.20% and silver slipped 0.83%. The numbers above are Wednesday's Treasury close, COMEX December gold and silver at the 4 PM ET print, and the ICE December Brent settlement.

CRYPTOCURRENCY

Bitcoin: $80,808 +0.06%  |  Ethereum: $2,338.80 -0.12%  |  XRP: $1.29 -2.09%

Calm after the Fed. Bitcoin is near $80,800, up 0.06% over 24 hours, Ether is down 0.12% and XRP is down 2.09%, live from CoinGecko at 11:23 AM PT. For once, the coins were steadier than the search engine.
